### D3 red team · Question

Event: `9f24ef8c33919e038b83f5fbed54cd09` · 2026-09-24T20:34:27Z

> Red-team review of D3 plan v1 (plan file wash-inbox-1-message-binary-scott.md) with the orchestrator's rulings on D3-plan. Read against BUILD-PLAN WP-D3 and WP-R3, IO-ARCHITECTURE (driver model, DMA, blkd, Networking), CONTAINMENT (sinks, channel table, crash blame), KERNEL-SPEC (R1, R3, R4, R4a, current call, mint), NAMESPACES /net, CAPABILITIES loopback login, and Q147. I also read the smoltcp 0.14.0 source in ~/.cargo/registry, the QEMU 10.2.2 man page (guestfwd), and testbench qemu.rs. Scope is clean: no kernel/, model/ or tests/programs/**, and the testbench overlap with K5 stays within the ruling.
> 
> VERDICT: BLOCK until v2 fixes P1-1 to P1-6. Every fix is a plan change with no new kernel feature. The P2 items are notes for v2.
> 
> == P1 ==
> P1-1 The bench peer does not count guest connections. The QEMU man page (-netdev user, guestfwd) says a chardev guestfwd `tcp:...-tcp:127.0.0.1:P` is opened at boot and 'used throughout QEMU's lifetime'. So the host peer sees one connection per forward at startup, whether the guest ever connects or connects many times. Consequences: `10.0.2.101:7 = 0` fails, or counts nothing real; `10.0.2.100 = 1` passes even if the guest never connected; the 'reaches nothing else' self-check and every attack verdict built on counts are not evidence. Fix: use the `guestfwd=tcp:ADDR:PORT-cmd:<helper>` form, which spawns a process per guest connection. The helper can be a testbench subcommand that echoes and reports to the bench. Add a must_fail twin in which the guest connects twice and the case expects 1, which proves the count really counts connections. This also removes the free_ports TOCTOU on the peer ports.
> 
> P1-2 The own-address boot sub-cases pass vacuously, so they catch no regression. With restrict=on, slirp drops every guest SYN except guestfwd matches, so 10.0.2.2:<hostfwd port>, 127.0.0.1 and 127.1.2.3 record 0 whether or not ipd checks. For 10.0.2.15 smoltcp ARPs for its own address and nobody answers. Fix: (a) give the rig's ipd `self=10.0.2.102/32` and guestfwd 10.0.2.102:7 to a counting helper, so a wide-scope attacker's connect must count 0, and a regression in self= or in 'self before scope' shows up as 1; (b) make the host end-to-end test the regression evidence: its link records every frame ipd emits and asserts no IPv4 destination in the self set and no ARP for a self address, under a 0.0.0.0/0 scope; (c) state in the plan which boot sub-cases are vacuous on slirp by construction.
> 
> P1-3 The QEMU self set is too narrow (3.4 and decision 6). libslirp sotranslate_out maps every address in the virtual network (10.0.2.0/24), except the DNS alias, to host loopback. It maps 10.0.2.3 to the host's resolver, often 127.0.0.53. Any non-vnet 127/8 or host address reaches the host directly. With restrict=off, each of those reaches the hostfwd back to the guest's sshd. The repo always sets restrict=on and binds hostfwd to 127.0.0.1, which closes this today; the gap is the manifest, which says `self=10.0.2.2/32`. Fix: the milestone QEMU manifest declares `self=10.0.2.0/24`, the bench rig uses its own narrower self= with the peers outside it, and the plan states that restrict=on is what closes slirp on the bench. Also state that the NAT-hairpin residual rests on sshd refusing keyd-held keys (CAPABILITIES; S3/E1), and that each ipd's self= must list every address of every ipd on the box (a follow-up for R3).
> 
> P1-4 The rx thread sends a physical address by message (section 1, 'the rx thread's one startup message, carrying the RX region's physical address'). The plan doesn't say how the serving thread authenticates it. consoled uses a fixed WAKE_BADGE=1. If netd copies that pattern and init mints a client handle with a colliding badge, the client can make netd program queue 0 with any physical address, and the device then DMAs network-controlled bytes anywhere in RAM. Fix: send no physical address at all. The serving thread dma_allocs both regions before thread_create and passes the rx region through an atomic written before the thread exists (consoled's WAKE_ENDPOINT precedent). BROKEN should arrive on a badge drawn from `random` above 2^63; netd must refuse `client=` equal to it; and nothing on that badge is accepted after DRIVER_OK except BROKEN.
> 
> P1-5 One packet from the network bricks the NIC. Section 1 treats a frame under 14 or over 1514 bytes as a device lie, which marks the device broken for good. On a tap or real LAN, an honest device delivers a peer's 1518-byte 802.1Q frame or a runt frame. Fix: distinguish a device lie (len > 2048, a bad or duplicate id, an idx jump, header flags or gso_type nonzero) from content netd doesn't accept (a frame length outside 14..1514 but within the buffer). The second case drops the frame and counts it, and the fuzz asserts that such a frame is not broken. Check num_buffers on QEMU before making any check on it strict.
> 
> P1-6 Q147 is understated for netd ('same as blkd'). blkd's device is idle between requests. netd always has 16 rx buffers posted, so after any netd death the next packet from the network is DMA'd into frames already returned to the pool: remote-controlled bytes in another process's (or the kernel's) memory. This needs the orchestrator to escalate Q147 (the kernel's reset-on-free recommendation) before netd restart or R3 use. Until then netd must reset the device (STATUS=0, then poll for 0) on every exit it controls and never free DMA regions while live. The residual is stated as a network-attacker write, not a device fault.
> 
> == P2 ==
> P2-1 TX stale-byte leak. The TX descriptor length is not specified. If it is a constant 2048, like the rx descriptors, the device sends trailing bytes of a previous frame to a new destination: Alice's traffic to A leaks to Bob's server B. The TX descriptor must be written for each transmit with len 12 + frame_len, and a host test should check the wire length.
> P2-2 ISN mitigation (the orchestrator asked for it). smoltcp can't be reseeded: Rand and InterfaceInner::rand are pub(crate), and random_seq_no is cx.rand().rand_u32(). PCG32 state is recoverable from one or two observed ISNs. Fork-free fix for outbound connections: Socket::connect(cx, remote, local) takes the Context, and with an explicit local address uses cx only for the ISN (tcp.rs:1013-1066). So ipd can pass the context() of a throwaway Interface::new(Config{random_seed: fresh kernel random}) for each connect, which makes outbound ISNs CSPRNG. Accepts still draw from the main Interface (tcp.rs:1919). Either rebuild the Interface with a fresh seed after each accept (the cost is re-ARPing the gateway) or state the residual precisely: listener ISNs are predictable, so an off-path attacker can complete a spoofed-source handshake (nothing trusts source IPs) or inject a reset or garbage, which SSH's MAC rejects (a DoS, not a compromise). A remote peer can also count the box-wide accept rate, a 'no global counters' channel among unlabelled users. Keep proto-ipv4-fragmentation off: the per-packet IPv4 ID counter exists only with it (ipv4.rs:33).
> P2-3 Crash blame. A thread's current call stays set while a call is parked or resumed; only a reply or a non-call receive clears it (KERNEL-SPEC current call). A smoltcp panic in the top-of-loop poll then blames the user whose read is parked, so three remote-triggered crashes destroy an innocent principal's budgets. Rule: run iface.poll only when the thread has no current call, which means ordering the loop so that a receive returning Timeout, Send or an abandoned notice precedes each poll. Test it on the host.
> P2-4 The labelled refusal is the only barrier to reads. The skeleton's check lets a caller labelled {7} read [] nodes ([] ⊆ {7}), which includes clone's read-to-allocate. So the refusal must live in a lib dispatch function that both the bin and the host tests use, not in bin/ipd.rs.
> P2-5 'Opens no bucket' is checked by an unchanged socket count from a control client, but 3.1 makes other connections' sockets invisible. Use bucket-slot exhaustion instead: buckets=K, the labelled attempt runs, then K distinct unlabelled accounts must all succeed. Give every attack case a positive control in the same boot (the victim accepts exactly one bench dial; an unlabelled twin with the same scope reaches the peer) and a distinct peer address per attacker, so counts can be attributed.
> P2-6 The listen-lineage rule is too coarse. The steward's root lineage covers every principal, so two principals granted the same port share it, and smoltcp hands a SYN to the first matching LISTEN socket (hijack). Key port ownership to the connection that first listened, plus its new_connection("") clones.
> P2-7 SYN flood. smoltcp's timeout moves SYN-RECEIVED to Closed, not back to LISTEN (tcp.rs:2470; only an RST re-listens, tcp.rs:1887), and with no timeout set, SYN-ACK retransmits forever. So ipd must set the timeout and re-listen by itself, without failing the holder's ctl read. Otherwise K spoofed SYNs every 10 s take sshd down. Consider 3 s and a larger K for sshd.
> P2-8 Socket numbers and ports. N must be per connection, not a global counter. Ephemeral ports must be unique among all live sockets, TIME-WAIT included, and must avoid listened ports: smoltcp doesn't check, and a duplicate tuple mixes users' segments.
> P2-9 A socket in TIME-WAIT, FIN-WAIT or a zero-window persist must stay charged until smoltcp actually frees it, and its linger must be bounded (set_timeout or keepalive). Otherwise close/disconnect churn holds uncharged 16 KiB sockets.
> P2-10 Sizing. in_flight 5 per bucket can't fit sshd (K parked listener ctl reads plus a data read and a Write::Wait per session). The steward's state 16 caps the box's concurrent /net grants. Size these, or state them (the CONTAINMENT sizing rule).
> P2-11 A lying device can boot-loop the box through ipd. smoltcp panics on a non-unicast MAC or address (interface/mod.rs:892, 899). netd must refuse a multicast or zero MAC at bring-up, and args must refuse a non-unicast addr=. ipd must not exit when netd answers `failed` (that means restarts, then init's reboot rule); it should stay up and answer `unreachable`.
> P2-12 The rig is a launcher, so it follows the WP-R3 placement rule (08848f60a): startup page and stack outside 0x1_0000..0x1FF0_0000, with a guard page.
> P2-13 The claim that the pre-K5 happy path needs no timers is wrong for smoltcp as configured: ack_delay defaults to 10 ms (tcp.rs:300). Use set_ack_delay(None), or verify.
> 
> == P3 ==
> - Supply chain: smoltcp's build.rs runs on the host and reads SMOLTCP_* environment variables, which change the compiled config; scrub them or assert none are set. Transitive dependencies are pinned only by Cargo.lock; add a check. Features unify through the host peer Interface's dev-dependency, so give the peer the identical feature set. heapless is used only as Vec and LinearMap, so read those and run Miri over the fuzz corpus.
> - Fuzz statefully (9P, ctl, frames and time together) with the invariants of P1-2b and charge balance, debug assertions on.
> - Grant: require canonical prefixes (host bits zero, len ≥ the held len). The ingress badge can't attach. Restrict new_connection paths to "" and "tcp", or specify socket delegation.
> - On target, give an attacker its scope through typed grant, not only through root arguments.
> - Derive the IRQ from the discovered slot rather than a constant 8 (P2-5's controls make a wrong pairing fail).
> - RST replies to broadcast-addressed SYNs, and 1:1 RST reflection: state them.
> 
> Checked and fine: IPv6 absent (no proto-ipv6); smoltcp drops TCP with an unspecified source or destination (interface/tcp.rs:13-21); the listener is bound to the interface address, so broadcast SYNs don't match; RFC 5961 challenge ACKs present; no ICMP echo or redirects; the ingress badge check; sends max_transfer=1; admission 40 ≤ 48; netd validates the used ring; the kind column and Write::Wait fit the rulings.

> P1-4: pass the RX region's address to the serving thread through state set before thread_create (an atomic or a startup word), not by an unauthenticated message. No badge can then inject a DMA address.
> P1-5: oversize or runt frames from the wire are DROPPED and counted, not treated as device lies. Only structural ring and descriptor violations are lies. A LAN packet must never brick the NIC.
> P1-6 (Q147): escalated. I'm flagging it to the owner as a kernel-level security gap: an always-armed rx device keeps writing peer bytes into DMA frames after netd dies, and those frames may be reused by other processes. D3 can't fix it without the kernel (K5 is the sole kernel writer). In D3: reset the device (STATUS=0) on every exit path netd controls, including panic; state the residual for kill and crash precisely; don't restart netd in any rig case. Also propose the kernel fix in the plan's open questions (e.g. a dma_alloc region's frames are quarantined, not reused, until the kernel resets or detaches the device the handle belongs to, or the kernel resets the device on its handle's release), for a follow-up kernel package after K5.
> P2s: take the red team's fixes. TX descriptor length is the frame length, never the slot, so no stale bytes. ISN: CSPRNG-seeded per connect via the throwaway Interface context, with the residual stated. Crash blame must not land on a parked caller during poll. Labelled refusal lives in the lib dispatch path (tested on host). Fix the no-bucket vs socket-visibility contradiction. Listen lineage goes finer (per root badge plus port). Re-listen after a SYN-RECEIVED timeout. N is per connection, and ephemeral ports are unique. Lingering sockets: say how their charge is bounded and released. in_flight sized for sshd. A non-unicast MAC is refused at startup, not a panic, and ipd exits with a code that won't reboot-loop. The rig follows the R3 placement rule (startup page and stack outside the stub's link range). ack_delay is fine pre-K5.
> P3s: take them (build.rs env, pinned transitive deps, feature unification, heapless audit plus Miri where feasible, stateful fuzz, canonical grants).

Event: `558683049243b9a9a76fc95583f867e1` · 2026-09-24T20:45:56Z

> Re-review of plan v2 (the v2 section of the plan file). I checked it against the smoltcp 0.14.0 source, libs/rt (admit.rs AdmitKey::of, the start.rs panic handler) and libslirp/QEMU behaviour.
> 
> VERDICT: OK with notes. Approve once the plan is consolidated with required edits R1-R5 below. None of them changes D3's design or needs a kernel change inside D3.
> 
> == Required in the consolidated plan ==
> R1. The Q147 residual is still understated. The '<= 16 frames, <= 32 KiB at fixed slot offsets' bound is wrong. The RX desc table and avail ring live in the freed RX region too. QEMU virtio-net re-reads avail.idx and the descriptors from guest memory each time a packet arrives (virtio_net_has_buffers, then virtqueue_pop), with no notify needed. So whoever next owns those frames, even an unprivileged process whose map_anon happens to get them, can post descriptors with any physical address, and the next LAN or broadcast frame is DMA'd there: an arbitrary physical write with sender-chosen bytes. The TX side is symmetric: an arbitrary read sent to the wire, if the device flushes or is kicked. Restate it that way. Consequence: the kernel quarantine is a prerequisite for any netd restart (R3) and for use off the bench. D3's bench acceptance can proceed with the residual stated. Notes for the kernel proposal:
> - quarantined frames stay charged (to the dead budget's parent or a kernel reserve) so nothing is overcommitted;
> - reset only devices the loader identified as virtio-mmio (magic and version), since the STATUS offset is virtio-specific;
> - a device that never acknowledges reset keeps its frames for ever (fail safe).
> The panic hook and the other orderly paths are good. Faults such as stack overflow skip the hook and remain the residual.
> 
> R2. The pcap assertion as written fails legitimate traffic, or will be relaxed ad hoc until it proves nothing. hostfwd connections arrive from 10.0.2.2, which is in the self set, so the guest's SYN-ACKs and data in d3-net-tcp (listen) and in any ssh case go to 10.0.2.2. State the rule as:
> - no guest-originated TCP SYN without ACK to a self_forbidden destination;
> - no guest-originated non-TCP IPv4 at all (ipd has none);
> - ARP only for the gateway.
> Classify 'guest-originated' as Ethernet source != slirp's 52:55:0a:00:02:02, which is fail-safe. Fail closed on a truncated, malformed or empty pcap: QEMU may be killed mid-record. Require the positive control's SYN to 10.0.9.100:7 to appear, which proves the capture is live. Derive self_forbidden from the same source as the rig's ipd self= arguments, or check the two are equal. With these, the pcap does prove that no connection attempt toward the self set left the guest NIC: filter-dump sits before slirp, so it sees SYNs that restrict=on later drops.
> 
> R3. The bucket-exhaustion control must prove the cap binds. In the same boot, after K distinct accounts succeed, a (K+1)-th must be refused. Otherwise an ignored buckets= (default 8) passes vacuously. Count every bucket alive at that moment: the rig's own granting badge is account 0 and holds state while its grants live, so it is a bucket too.
> 
> R4. Admission overrides.
> (a) AdmitKey::of uses the raw caller.badge for account 0, so an override applies only to calls on that exact root badge. A connection sshd or the steward mints for itself is a separate default bucket and uses a slot. State that both call on their root badges, or extend the override.
> (b) Apply an override only when caller.account == 0 (ipd can't know a badge's account at parse time). Refuse override badges >= 2^63 and duplicates.
> (c) Startup totals must be sum(overrides) + (buckets - #overrides) x default, both <= 48 and fits.
> The manifest table's 24 + 4x6 = 48 leaves out the steward's own bucket (a sixth), so the arithmetic needs fixing. With (a)-(c), a misconfiguration either fails closed at startup or changes only the misnamed badge's own cap, and isolation between buckets holds.
> 
> R5. Consolidate the file into one clean plan with an OWNER DECISIONS section. The file currently layers v2 dispositions over the v1 body, whose decisions 6 and 11 and parts of sections 1, 3, 5 and 6 are superseded.
> 
> == Verified closed (with small notes) ==
> - P1-1: closed with the cmd: helper. Note: an O_EXCL name of <addr>.<pid> can collide on pid reuse and undercount (the twice twin). Use a unique suffix with a retry, and have the helper refuse to echo if it can't record.
> - /16 layout: the milestone manifest keeps slirp's default /24, which self=10.0.2.0/24 covers fully (vhost .2, DNS .3, every other address). In peer cases the rest of 10.0.0.0/16 maps to host loopback only when restrict is off, and restrict=on is what closes it. Add a qemu.rs unit test asserting that every [net] case emits restrict=on, because the /16 widens the loopback-mapped space.
> - P1-2: the self-unrefused twin catches a missing self check. 'Misordered' overclaims, which is harmless.
> - P1-4: closed. No message carries an address; BROKEN has a random badge and no data; client= is below 2^63. Note: if thread_create fails, reclaim the Box with from_raw and don't retry with it; add the unsafe-budget entry.
> - P1-5: closed.
> - rt panic hook: minimal and acceptable if:
>   - it runs before report_panic, which can block for PANIC_TIMEOUT on the console call;
>   - it has its own once-flag, so a panic inside the hook skips it and exits;
>   - set_panic_hook is set-once;
>   - the hook is bounded and doesn't allocate;
>   - the fn-pointer storage's unsafe is counted in rt's budget.
>   Panic-to-process_exit is unchanged. It goes in the shared-runtime review with Write::Wait, mint_rooted and the Admission override.
> - ISN: verified. Connect and passive open both draw CSPRNG ISNs per connection. poll_ingress_single sends replies (RST, challenge ACK) through the throwaway Interface's empty neighbour cache: they may be lost, as stated, which is acceptable. Add:
>   - if random fails, drop the SYN or refuse the connect, never fall back to the main PRNG;
>   - pass an explicit local address to connect.
>   IPv4 ident is 0 (wire/ipv4.rs:604), confirmed.
> - P2-3: fine. A reply also clears the current call, so receive(0) is needed only after a park, or after a resumed call that parks again.
> - No-link mode: fail-closed and sound. Specify:
>   - it is entered only when info fails, the MAC is not unicast, or transmit answers `failed`; never on Timeout or busy;
>   - info is retried with backoff, so a restarted netd recovers;
>   - every check stays in force.
> - P2-6 to P2-13 and P3: closed. P2-13 is accepted.
> 
> == P3 additions ==
> - Drop inbound TCP whose source is ipd's own address, 127/8 or 0/8 (not 10.0.2.2, where hostfwd arrives).
> - Give attacker and labelled programs no console handle, and anchor verdict lines to the rig's prefix.
> - Scope is still clean: nothing in kernel/, model/ or K5's paths.
